oewn-01229679-n.learner: the act of forgiving someone for a mistake or a wrong.
examples: He begged pardon for having displeased her.
"I beg your pardon," replied Miss Bingley, turning away with a sneer.

oewn-06564630-n.learner: an official paper that frees a person from being punished for a crime.
examples: The king signed a pardon for the prisoner.

oewn-01251862-n.learner: the official act of setting a person free.
examples: The new government granted a pardon to everyone who had been jailed.

oewn-10343292-n.learner: a woman who is in charge and tells other people what work to do.
examples: it is very hard to think that Charlotte Lucas should ever be mistress of this house
she was selected from among her sisters as worthy of being the mistress of Hunsford Parsonage

oewn-10343410-n.learner: a woman who is unfaithful in marriage; a woman who keeps up a sexual relationship with a man she is not married to.
examples: He kept a mistress in town for years while his wife stayed in the country.

connotation.why: names a woman by a sexual role held to be improper

oewn-10579268-n.learner: a woman who teaches in a school, above all one seen as strict.
examples: The mistress silenced the whole class with one look.

connotation.why: carries a picture of the teacher as harsh

oewn-08682181-n.learner: a point in a region, fixed by what lies on the surface around it.
examples: she saw and admired every remarkable spot and point of view
Her thoughts were all fixed on that one spot of Pemberley House, whichever it might be

oewn-04689819-n.learner: a small part of something that looks different from the rest of it.
examples: A white spot marked the horse's forehead.

oewn-04701789-n.learner: a mark left on something by dirt.
examples: She rubbed at a greasy spot on her sleeve.

oewn-01515272-s.learner: as great in degree, size, or strength as it can possibly be.
examples: He answered me with the utmost civility
The idea of his returning no more Elizabeth treated with the utmost contempt.

oewn-00445635-s.learner: furthest away in space, in time, or in order.
examples: A single light burned at the utmost end of the pier.

oewn-00728262-v.learner: to say that something comes from, or is owed to, a certain person or thing.
examples: a dislike which I cannot but attribute in some measure to jealousy
Something, he supposed, might be attributed to his connection with them

oewn-00742058-v.learner: to work out where something belongs within an ordered set of classes.
examples: Experts attribute the vase to the early Ming period.

oewn-02317976-v.learner: to free someone from a load, a harm, or a trouble.
examples: the boys were relieved from their apprehension of Charlotte's dying an old maid
the business of love-making relieved them from a great deal of his company

oewn-01819152-v.learner: to make something weaker, or to make it quiet down.
examples: Her curiosity, however, was unexpectedly relieved.

oewn-00063866-v.learner: to ease something felt in the body, such as pain.
examples: A cold cloth relieved the ache in her head.

oewn-13804245-n.learner: the tie between you and someone who has done you a favour or a service, so that you owe them.
examples: they were under obligations to a person who could never receive a return
the obligations which Mr. Gardiner's behaviour laid them all under

oewn-01132241-n.learner: the pull of other people that ties you to the actions it asks of you.
examples: A sense of obligation kept him at his post long after the others had gone home.

oewn-14513694-n.learner: the state of having to do something or pay something.
examples: She was under an obligation to repay the loan by June.
Mrs. Collins's pretty friend had, moreover, caught his fancy very much
Lizzy does not lose much by not suiting his fancy

oewn-05640055-n.learner: the power of making pictures in the mind, which Coleridge held to be lighter and less deep than true imagination.
examples: In her fancy the old house stood just as it had in her childhood.

oewn-05904666-n.learner: a belief that many people hold but that is not true.
examples: The notion that lightning never strikes the same place twice is an old fancy.

connotation.why: sets a shared belief aside as untrue
